newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sets May 29 for 1997 general elections.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sets May 29 for 1997 general elections.

text.p: Indonesia's General Election Institute (LPU) has set May 29 as the date for next year's general elections, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.
Campaigning will be allowed officially between April 29 and May 23, with a cooling-off period of five days before the polling day itself, the agency said.

Only three parties are legally allowed to contest the 425 elective places in the 500-seat parliament: the ruling Golkar party, the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
The remaining 75 seats are nominated by the country's powerful military.
In the last elections in 1992, Golkar took 68 percent of the vote, the PPP 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
